digest.component_or_area: S3 remote store doctor / multi-bundle reconciliation
propositions: When two or more git bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git ls-remote returns the ref at multiple SHAs and a fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable.
The push path stalls: git-remote-s3 cmd_push rejects with 'multiple bundles exists on server' before writing anything, and rebar's fetch cannot resolve the ambiguous ref, so retries never converge.

Upstream's interactive git_remote_s3.Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is unusable for autonomous fleets: it blocks on input() prompts which crash on EOF, and discards the non-chosen head's unique events rather than merging them, causing data loss in an append-only event log.

Rebar already implements lossless multi-parent merge reconciliation for ordinary git remotes in sync.py _do_reconverge/_union_merge, reusing .gitattributes merge=ours for derived .bridge_state/* and UUID-named event dirs that never collide; the S3 multi-bundle case is ordinary ref divergence hidden at the bundle-storage layer.

The heal must write the merged bundle before deleting any original bundle and never delete the merged bundle, ensuring at least one lossless bundle survives every crash point (before merge=done leaves N originals; mid-delete leaves merged + subset of originals; post-delete leaves only merged).

On a genuine non-derived-file conflict the heal aborts without deleting any remote bundle, releases all locks, leaves the remote untouched, and surfaces rebar fsck-recover rather than silently discarding a parent.
